alex: quick question — ran a short nsys capture and the kernel timeline shows big gaps and several tiny kernels missing. cmd I used:

```
nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=3s ./inference_bin --batch 1
```

Is this expected with OSRT + sampling?

mira: yep. OSRT schedules a lot of very short kernels. If your sampling interval is coarser than those tiny launches you'll miss them. Short duration makes it worse.

ben: two practical options: `--sample=none` to get event-based tracing (bigger file, but you won't miss kernels), or keep sampling but increase resolution. Also bracket the steady-state with NVTX and use `--capture-range=nvtx` so you only capture the hot loop.

alex: thanks — any recommended numbers for sampling or duration?

sam: if you must sample, bump the resolution e.g. `--sample=cpu:100us` or use `--sample-freq` (depends on nsys version). I usually run 6-12s for steady-state captures on CI to avoid warmup noise.

mira: alternate flow: do a short warmup loop (no capture) then trigger a longer capture window. Bracketing with NVTX is the least noisy. Also note nvtx itself adds tiny overhead so don't bracket single-shot ops.

ben: also be aware OSRT may aggregate or reorder tiny kernel launches; the timeline can look like gaps while the runtime batches things. Enabling extra cuda activity flags helps: `--cuda-memory-activity=true --cuda-kernel-nvtx=true`.

alex: got it. any tips for CLI to keep files manageable?

mira: `--capture-range=nvtx` + `--sample=none` plus capturing only the inner loop usually keeps sizes sane. Or capture a few iterations with sampling high-res if you need stacks, then `nsys stats` to summarize hotspots.

ben: and if you need source-symbol mapping use `--source-level` and build with debug symbols for the kernels you want to inspect.

infra-bot: build #6421 finished — nsys v2023.4 image available as redwood/inference:ci-2023-6421

alex: I'll rerun with `--sample=none` + nvtx bracketing and post the .nsys output.

alex: attaching the nvtx wrapper we use in the runtime to bracket inference loops:

```
// C++ pseudo
nvtxRangePushA("infer-loop");
for (int i=0; i < iters; ++i) run_one_batch();
nvtxRangePop();
```

mira: perfect. when you share the capture, run `nsys stats out.nsys` first — it gives a quick top-k by GPU time. saves a lot of timeline digging.

alex: will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
